title: Analytics & observability subsystem
purpose: A self-contained observability subsystem providing event-driven metric collection, thread-safe SQLite persistence, threshold-based alerting, CPU/RAM monitoring, dashboard payload generation, and Markdown/JSON reports for the campus helpdesk, explicitly designed for low-memory Raspberry Pi deployment. It is the dormant analytics layer: fully implemented, self-consistent, and unit/integration tested, but nothing in the production application/ or api/ layers currently publishes events to it, so it records no data during normal operation.

files.purpose: Package re-export module that imports and declares the public API of every analytics module so consumers can `from campus_helpdesk.analytics import AnalyticsManager` etc.
files.notes: Pure re-export module with no logic. Exposes 12 classes; the module docstring is a compact index of the subsystem.

files.purpose: Threshold-based alerting engine that subscribes to analytics events, persists raised alerts to the MetricsStore `alerts` table, publishes an AlertRaised event, and enforces a per-type cooldown to prevent alert storms.

terms.definition: A configured numeric limit (latency, score, CPU/RAM, hallucination rate); when a metric crosses it the engine raises an alert.
The minimum interval (default 60s) enforced between repeated alerts of the same alert_type to prevent alert storms; a raise inside the cooldown is suppressed.
Categorical label for a raised alert: HighLatency, LowRetrievalQuality, HighHallucinationRate, or SystemResourceWarning.
Alert priority classification; all alerts in this engine are raised at WARNING.

config: thresholds dict (constructor override of DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS: retrieval_latency_sec, llm_latency_sec, end_to_end_latency_sec, memory_mb, cpu_percent, hallucination_rate, min_retrieval_score)
files.notes: get_active_alert_count reaches into store._lock and store._conn private attributes (tight coupling). Several DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS keys are never checked: only end_to_end_latency_sec (from QueryCompleted payload latency_ms), min_retrieval_score (from RetrievalCompleted metadata), and cpu_percent/memory_mb (from SystemMetricRecorded) are used; retrieval_latency_sec, llm_latency_sec, and hallucination_rate have no corresponding handler. Alert raise happens under a lock but publishing occurs outside it. Bounded in-memory recent buffer capped at 100.

files.purpose: Central orchestrator that constructs a MetricsStore and EventBus, wires every analytics module and the AlertEngine as bus subscribers, runs a background worker queue plus PerformanceMonitor, and exposes facade methods for dashboards, alerts, reports, and combined stats.

terms.definition: One user query within a conversation session; a turn's query/retrieval/latency/quality data is persisted as one analytics record.
A convenience method on the manager (get_dashboard, get_alerts, generate_report, get_all_stats) that hides wiring and returns aggregated results to callers.

files.notes: Two parallel ingestion paths: (1) publish_event fans out to EventBus subscribers (QueryAnalytics, RetrievalAnalytics, etc.); (2) track_turn enqueues a legacy dict that the AnalyticsWorker thread persists via _persist. The same query can therefore be written to query_logs twice (once by the QueryAnalytics handler, once by _persist) if a caller uses both. _persist calls store.prune_old every turn. Worker and perf threads are daemons; stop() unblocks the worker with a sentinel None. No production code in src/ instantiates or calls this class; it is used only by tests and the scripts/verify_project.py import smoke test.

files.purpose: Subscribes to SessionStarted/SessionEnded/TurnCompleted events and tracks session duration, turns per session, topic distribution, and engagement, persisting session lifecycle records to MetricsStore.

terms.definition: A conversation identified by session_id with a start and end time; analytics measures its duration and turn count.
A free-form category label attached to a turn via event metadata (default 'general'), aggregated into a topic_distribution.

files.notes: All aggregate counters are in-memory only, capped at _max_history=500; session start/end/turn events are also persisted to MetricsStore. handle_session_ended persists an end_time even when no matching active session exists (session_data is None), and handle_turn_completed calls update_session_end for unknown session_ids, which no-ops since no row matches. No constructor config keys; store and event_bus are injected.

files.purpose: Stateless generator that queries MetricsStore tables and returns a structured JSON dashboard payload (summary, latency, quality, system health, recent queries) for a Tkinter dashboard view or future web UI.

terms.definition: Latency value at the 50th/90th/99th sorted rank of sampled end_to_end latencies, used to summarize the response-time distribution.
The fraction of query_logs rows with status='success' within the time window, reported by the dashboard summary.
The fraction of quality_logs rows with hallucination_flag set within the time window, reported as avg_unsupported/hallucination_rate.

files.notes: Docstring mentions a 'Tkinter dashboard view' that does not exist in the repo, and a 'future web UI'; nothing in src/ consumes DashboardGenerator output. _get_system_health ignores its cutoff argument (returns the single latest row overall). Percentiles use an approximate nearest-rank index (int(n*0.5)) with no interpolation. All queries go through store._lock/_conn private attributes instead of MetricsStore's public fetchall helpers.

files.purpose: Thread-safe in-process publish/subscribe event bus where each published event invokes all registered handlers, each in its own daemon thread so publishing never blocks the main pipeline.

terms.definition: An in-process pub/sub mechanism where modules register handler callables for named events and publishers fire them without knowing the subscribers.
A callable registered on the bus for a named event (e.g. RetrievalCompleted); it receives the event payload when the event is published.

files.notes: publish() starts one new daemon thread per handler per event — unbounded thread creation and no delivery ordering guarantee, so handlers can race with state the publisher just wrote. subscribe/unsubscribe are guarded by an RLock but handlers are copied under lock and run outside it. No backpressure or error reporting back to the publisher.

files.purpose: Subscribes to RetrievalCompleted and QueryFailed events and tracks document/chunk access frequency, detects knowledge gaps (low-score or failed queries), and collects unknown questions with bounded memory.

terms.definition: A question whose retrieval score is below 0.3 or whose query failed, flagged as evidence the knowledge base cannot answer it.
A segment of a knowledge document that the retriever returns; chunks are tracked individually by chunk_id for utilisation analysis.
A collected low-score or failed user query retained (bounded at 200) as evidence of a knowledge gap, exposed via get_unknown_questions.

files.notes: Module docstring claims state is persisted to MetricsStore, but all state is in-memory only; no MetricsStore write methods are called. The knowledge-gap threshold 0.3 is hardcoded and duplicates AlertEngine's min_retrieval_score default with no shared configuration. get_least_accessed_documents only surfaces documents that were accessed at least once (never the unaccessed corpus). The _max_unknown bounded list is FIFO (pop(0)).

files.purpose: Thread-safe SQLite persistence layer owning the schema for all analytics tables (sessions, query_logs, retrieval_logs, latency_logs, quality_logs, system_metrics, alerts, pipeline_traces) with insert/query helpers and retention pruning.

terms.definition: Per-turn row recording query_id, session_id, raw/resolved query, intent, status ('success'/'fallback'/'failed'), and follow-up/topic-switch flags.
Per-turn row of stage latencies in ms (query_understanding, retrieval, reranking, llm_generation, validation, end_to_end).
Per-turn row of confidence_score, hallucination_flag, citation_coverage, and unsupported_rate.
Deleting rows older than a retention window (default 30 days) from prunable tables, then VACUUMing to reclaim space.

config: db_path constructor argument (database_path from AnalyticsManager config)
files.notes: Single sqlite3 connection opened with check_same_thread=False and guarded by a threading.Lock, so the background worker and monitor threads share one connection. query_logs.status has a CHECK constraint restricting values to success/fallback/failed. Dependent tables without a timestamp column (retrieval_logs, latency_logs, quality_logs) are pruned via a subquery JOIN on query_logs. Timestamps are stored as naive SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP-format strings though computed with datetime.now(UTC). VACUUM is skipped for :memory: databases and on any exception.

files.purpose: Background daemon thread that periodically samples CPU and RAM utilisation — reading /proc/stat and /proc/meminfo directly on Linux/Raspberry Pi with cross-platform fallbacks — and persists snapshots to system_metrics using zero external dependencies (no psutil).

terms.definition: Periodic cpu_percent and ram_used_mb snapshots persisted to the system_metrics table and consumed by dashboard/report/alert consumers.
Linux kernel virtual file whose first 'cpu' line is read twice 100 ms apart; the idle/total deltas yield instantaneous CPU percentage.
Linux kernel virtual file from which used RAM is computed as MemTotal minus MemAvailable (kB converted to MB).

config: interval_seconds constructor argument (system_monitor_interval_seconds from AnalyticsManager config, default 10)
files.notes: On Windows (the primary dev platform) both fallbacks silently return 0.0: os.getloadavg raises AttributeError and the resource module is unavailable, so no real system metrics are collected on Windows and CPU/RAM alerts never fire there. CPU reading is instantaneous (aggregate across all cores), not an averaged interval load. start() is idempotent; stop() joins with a timeout of interval+2s. The _read_cpu_percent_linux fallback to _read_cpu_percent_fallback path is only used on non-Linux platforms.

files.purpose: Utility providing a new UUIDv4 trace_id per pipeline turn and a normalized event_payload dict that all analytics modules expect when publishing events on the EventBus.

terms.definition: A UUIDv4 uniquely identifying one pipeline turn, carried on every event payload so events from different components (QueryReceived, RetrievalCompleted, etc.) can be linked to the same turn.
The standardized dict (trace_id, session_id, turn_id, timestamp, component, event_type, latency_ms, metadata, severity) that analytics handlers read and persist.

files.notes: event_payload uses datetime.utcnow() (deprecated, naive UTC) while every other module in the package uses datetime.now(UTC), producing inconsistent timestamp tz-awareness. The severity field defaults to 'INFO' but the engine only ever raises WARNING alerts. Payload keys intentionally use trace_id as the query identifier (see QueryAnalytics which persists payload.trace_id as query_id).

files.purpose: Subscribes to QueryReceived/QueryCompleted/QueryFailed events and tracks intent distribution, status breakdown, follow-up rate, and topic-switch rate, persisting each completed or failed query to query_logs.

terms.definition: A category label for a query taken from event metadata (default 'unknown'), aggregated into intent_distribution.
Query outcome label ('success', 'failed', or schema-allowed 'fallback') aggregated into status_distribution and persisted to query_logs.
Fractions of queries flagged has_followup / topic_switched, divided by the total query count (which can push them above 1.0).

files.notes: Persists payload.trace_id as query_id, so every traced turn produces a query_logs row. handle_query_failed hardcodes status='failed' and forces has_followup/topic_switched to False. get_stats divides followup and topic-switch counts by the QueryReceived total, so a session that also emits QueryCompleted/QueryFailed events can yield followup_rate or topic_switch_rate greater than 1.0. In-memory counters are reset only by reset(); get_stats does not clear them despite its docstring phrasing.

files.purpose: Produces Markdown and JSON summary reports (daily, weekly, or arbitrary custom windows) from MetricsStore and DashboardGenerator data, written to a configurable output directory.

terms.definition: A timestamped Markdown plus JSON pair summarizing dashboard data (summary, latency, quality, system health), alerts, and intent distribution over a time window.

config: output_dir constructor argument (report_output_dir from AnalyticsManager config, default data/analytics/reports)
files.notes: The module docstring says reports can be 'scheduled for daily/weekly summaries', but no scheduler exists anywhere in the repo — generation is strictly on-demand via generate_daily_report/generate_weekly_report/generate_custom_report. _get_alerts and _get_intent_distribution reach into store._lock/_conn directly. JSON output is dumped with default=str. Filenames embed the UTC timestamp (report_{label}_{YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS}.md/.json). Markdown render formats success_rate as a percentage that was already rounded to 4 decimals.

files.purpose: Subscribes to RetrievalCompleted events and tracks retrieval quality indicators — scores, chunk hits, cross-encoder scores, and unused-document counts — in bounded in-memory buffers while persisting each retrieval to retrieval_logs.

terms.definition: The retriever's quality score (0..1) attached to a RetrievalCompleted event, averaged over a bounded buffer for stats.
The reranker (cross-encoder) relevance score attached to a RetrievalCompleted event, tracked separately from the retrieval score.
The number of retrieved documents not used in the final answer, recorded as a retrieval quality indicator.
A chunk_id appearing in a RetrievalCompleted payload's retrieved_chunk_ids; each occurrence is tallied in _chunk_hits for utilisation analysis.

files.notes: In-memory running buffers are capped at 500 entries using list pop(0) (ring-buffer style). The unused_docs buffer records 0 for every event even when no unused-docs value is supplied, so avg_unused_docs counts all retrievals. Persistence uses payload.trace_id as query_id, consistent with QueryAnalytics. Module docstring notes the low-memory footprint design for Raspberry Pi.

data_flow: Fully self-contained and currently unwired into production. AnalyticsManager is the only entry point: it creates a MetricsStore (SQLite at data/analytics/metrics.sqlite) and an EventBus, constructs QueryAnalytics, RetrievalAnalytics, ConversationAnalytics, KnowledgeAnalytics, and AlertEngine as bus subscribers, and starts a daemon AnalyticsWorker thread (turn queue) plus a PerformanceMonitor thread. Two ingestion paths exist: (1) publish_event(event_name, payload) fans a payload out to all bus subscribers; (2) track_turn(turn_data) enqueues a legacy dict that the worker persists via _persist (sessions, query_logs, and optional retrieval/latency/quality logs, then prune_old). Payloads are standardized by PipelineTrace.event_payload/new_trace_id (trace_id is used as query_id downstream). Consumption is via façade methods — DashboardGenerator.generate produces the dashboard JSON, ReportGenerator.generate_* writes Markdown+JSON reports, AlertEngine.get_recent_alerts/get_active_alert_count surface alerts — all querying the same MetricsStore. Event names form a de-facto contract: QueryReceived/QueryCompleted/QueryFailed, RetrievalCompleted, SessionStarted/SessionEnded/TurnCompleted, SystemMetricRecorded, AlertRaised. Nothing in application/ or api/ currently calls AnalyticsManager or publish_event, so the only live consumers are tests (tests/unit/test_analytics_modules.py, tests/integration/test_analytics_integration.py) and the import smoke check in scripts/verify_project.py; in normal API operation all analytics tables stay empty.
external_deps: Python standard library only: sqlite3, threading, queue, uuid, json, logging, pathlib, platform, os, time, resource, collections, datetime (timezone-aware UTC for store/modules; naive datetime.utcnow in pipeline_trace)
risks: Dormant / unwired: nothing in src/campus_helpdesk/application/ or api/ publishes analytics events or instantiates AnalyticsManager, so the subsystem records no production data and all metrics tables remain empty during normal operation.

EventBus.publish spawns a new daemon thread per handler per event — unbounded thread creation, no delivery ordering, and handler errors are swallowed (only logged by the handler) with no backpressure to the publisher.

Private-internal coupling: DashboardGenerator, ReportGenerator, and AlertEngine.get_active_alert_count read and write MetricsStore._lock/_conn directly instead of using its public fetchall/fetchone/execute API, creating a refactoring hazard and bypassing the store's access discipline.

PerformanceMonitor returns 0.0 CPU/RAM on Windows (the primary dev platform) because os.getloadavg raises AttributeError and the resource module is unavailable — so system_health and SystemResourceWarning alerts are effectively dead on Windows.

AlertEngine default thresholds include keys with no checking handler (retrieval_latency_sec, llm_latency_sec, hallucination_rate), and the knowledge-gap threshold 0.3 is hardcoded in knowledge_analytics separately from AlertEngine's min_retrieval_score default.
Double-logging: a turn fed through both track_turn and the EventBus path writes query_logs twice (once via the QueryAnalytics handler, once via the worker's _persist), skewing dashboard counts.

Rate math can exceed 1.0: QueryAnalytics divides follow-up and topic-switch counts by the QueryReceived total, so sessions emitting separate completed/failed events push followup_rate/topic_switch_rate above 100%.

Inconsistent timestamp handling: pipeline_trace uses deprecated naive datetime.utcnow() while all other modules use datetime.now(UTC); MetricsStore stores timestamps as naive CURRENT_TIMESTAMP-format strings.

Legacy dual-path design (track_turn queue vs EventBus) and a Tkinter dashboard that does not exist in the repo indicate the subsystem was built ahead of its consumers; the ReportGenerator 'scheduled daily/weekly' claim has no scheduler implementation.
